text:
santiago: Heads up — during the eu-west2 nightly batch window we saw NVMe write latency crater and a correlated spike in GPU provisioning failures (~30% launch retries). Suspect scrub + janitor overlap with provisioning.

maya: ugh that timing again. any logs?

santiago: logs show heavy fsync bursts from scrub workers and a ton of queue depth on /dev/nvme0n1. iostat snapshot: `rkB/s` jumps and `await` goes >200ms for short periods.

aj: can you paste the exact scrub cron? last time we had overlapping windows because the scrub backoff didn't respect launch pressure.

santiago: here:```
0 3 * * * /usr/local/bin/ephemeral-scrub --rate=200 --max-concurrent=6
```
we had autoscaling for GPUs trying to spin up at 3:00 and scrub concurrent=6 saturated the drives.

infra-bot: alert: nvme_io_wait_high on gnode-eu-west2-** at 2025-08-06T03:01:12Z (latency >150ms)

katie: quick mitigation: reduce scrub concurrency to 1-2 or add a cgroup io weight so scrub yields to provisioning. also consider moving scrub window outside peak provisioning.

devon: cgroup io_weight might be faster to roll. weight=100 for scrub, weight=1000 for kubelet pods? we can tune via systemd slice for janitor.

maya: agree. but i worry about long-term wear: if we keep pushing scrubs later we bunch them and cause a bigger pulse. maybe we need a fair-share scrub scheduler that respects ongoing provisioning pressure (feedback loop).

aj: proposal: implement a simple token-bucket in the scrub controller: tokens minted by time, but drain when host io_wait exceeds threshold. scrub reduces concurrency automatically. low-effort deploy.

santiago: sounds good. also we should add a short-term workaround: patch the gpu-provisioner to prefer nodes with lower nvme_iops_util and avoid nodes with active scrub jobs. That avoids immediate launch failures while we fix scrub controller.

katie: +1. i'll open a rollout PR for the kube scheduler predicate and a hotfix to the scrub systemd unit to cap concurrency to 2 for the night window.

devon: also flag: consider adding `--write-bandwidth-limit` (bytes/s) to scrubs so it's not just concurrent jobs but absolute throughput cap. some NVMe models behave worse at high QD than others.

santiago: good point. let's do two things: 1) immediate: scheduler predicate + systemd cap; 2) medium: token-bucket scrub controller + io-weight tuning; 3) long: add telemetry to correlate scrub operations with GPU launch SLOs and create automatic delay when launch failure rate > 5%.

aj: fwiw, we saw similar in us-west2 but it became a tail issue after firmware push — different symptom but same root: local disk work competing with provisioning. worth adding a canary that simulates launch traffic while scrubs run.

maya: can someone file a quick incident note? i'll add runbook steps for mitigation (cap, weight, exclude nodes).

santiago: filing note now. cc @katie @aj for PRs. thanks. :thumbsup:

infra-bot: incident-created: INCIDENT-2025-0812-NVME-SCRUB-EVIC (priority: P2)

katie: i'll take the scheduler PR, aj take the scrub controller patch, devon do the cgroup/weight changes, maya update runbook. santiago will monitor rollout.

santiago: monitoring: setting alert to 10% launch retry within 5m and nvme await >100ms. will revert caps if rollout causes other regressions.

devon: can we add an exporter metric from the janitor: `scrub_io_bytes_total` and `scrub_inflight_jobs`? makes thresholds easier.

aj: yep will add in scrub v0.7.1.

maya: thanks all — feel better having an action plan.

santiago: closing loop: will post postmortem if we hit the incident threshold or if mitigation changes are required.
